**Title:** Same Name, Different Unit: Identifying Source-Specific Units in Web Price Fusion

**Abstract (299 words):**

Price aggregators, indexes and oracles combine prices from many web sources and assume that every source's dollar is the same dollar. Often it is not. A crypto exchange's dollar balance is a claim on that exchange, and it can lose value when the exchange's banking breaks down. An aggregator then mistakes a change in the dollar for a change in price. We detect this from public prices. When an exchange's dollar moves, every asset on that exchange moves by the same amount, so the part of the price gaps that all assets share measures the dollar's offset. A stablecoin traded on the exchange, corrected for its own price elsewhere, then separates a move in the dollar from demand for the assets. We give an identification result, a moment-based test and a simulation of its size and power. Flowerday et al. (2026) proposed that Bitfinex's 2018–19 premium reflected a discount on its dollar but could not test it. From November 2018 to May 2019, once Tether's own price on Kraken was netted out, Bitfinex's Tether price tracked its dollar offset with slope 0.97 (95% interval 0.94 to 1.00), up from 0.71: the offset moved close to one for one with Bitfinex's dollar. Binance.US in 2023 gave a slope of 1.00, close to mechanical once its deposits closed, though a two-stablecoin version of the test rejected. On assets kept out of development, one offset per exchange and hour removed 0.989 of the squared price gap in 2017–19 and 0.353 in 2020–23. A plain median was hard to beat in three one-shot fusion tests. In a pre-registered test on new events, where most trading shared one stablecoin that lost its peg, a frozen unit-aware method beat the median, stablecoin conversion and source-reliability weighting (CRH), and narrowly beat a median of dollar-quoted markets.

**Suggested keywords:** exchange dollars; unit of account; truth discovery; price feeds and oracles; Web data quality; cryptocurrency markets; reproducibility
